newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures end flat, belie jumpy session.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures end flat, belie jumpy session.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures closed unchanged, belying a jumpy session that saw December T-bonds rally near 116-00 after the opening and then fall near key support in the final minutes of trade.
"It's important that we close above 115-02/32," Barrett Lewald, senior financial futures strategist at Lind-Waldock Inc, said during the session.

The likelihood of December bonds falling through 115-02/32 increased late in the day, as the contract sold off to a day's low of 115-03/32 near the close of pit trade, which was at 1210 CST/1810 GMT. Eurodollars ended trade at 1200 CST/1800 GMT.
However, December bonds limited losses at 115-03/32 ahead of what will be a four-day holiday weekend for many traders and dealers in the U.S.
U.S. bonds and Euros will be closed on Thursday for the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, and Friday's trade will end at 1210 CST/1810 GMT for bonds and 1200 CST/1800 GMT for Euros.
Profit-taking turned heavy after most of the U.S. economic reports released on Wednesday morning indicated that growth in the fourth quarter was slightly stronger than anticipated.
Bonds and Euros have been pricing in an economic slowdown, with some traders expecting an eventual easing of U.S. rates.

"We're having a hard time here for good reason," Lewald said. "The economy is slowing down from its breakneck pace, but I wonder if we can move higher without clear signs of weaker U.S. economic growth."

October durable goods orders rose 0.1 percent in October, against the average trade estimate for a 2.0 percent decline. Orders excluding defense were up 0.4 percent, compared to forecasts for a drop of 2.2 percent.
"Durable goods was a little disturbing, but it's not exactly a robust number either," Lewald said. September durable goods orders were revised downward to a 4.6 percent gain.
The Chicago purchasing managers index rose to 57.6 in November, compared to the average trade forecast of 55.1 and against October's 56.9.
One trader said a major U.S. firm immediately sold 600 December bonds off the Chicago index.
University of Michigan's final consumer sentiment survey for November was also higher, rising to 99.2, against estimates of 98 and against October's final reading of 96.5.
The economic figures led weak longs to reconsider the prospects for a slowdown in the fourth quarter.
"It really took the froth out of the market," one Eurodollar futures trader said. Earlier in the session, March rose to 94.54, scaling above resistance at 94.52.
However, traders said continued demand from foreign investors and domestic money managers, who may be looking to extend duration on portfolios, could keep the market well supported in the near term.
At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were off 01/32 at 115-10/32, 10-year notes were up 01/32 at 110-31/32, and March and June Eurodollars closed unchanged at 94.51 and 94.42.
